## Natural history notes

A small leaf beetle characterized by its yellow-green wing covers marked with distinct black spots, a dark head, and long slender antennae. In Florida, it is found in gardens, farms, fields, roadsides, parks, and other open habitats where cucurbits, corn, beans, and many other host plants grow. Adults feed on leaves, flowers, pollen, and fruit surfaces, while the larvae live in the soil and feed on roots; this species can be an agricultural pest but also serves as prey for birds, spiders, assassin bugs, and other predators.
